Commentary.Commentary: The Zimbabwean players get into a huddle. Charlton Tshuma gets his debut Test cap, amidst a small procession. Now, out come the batsmen. Saif Hassan and Tamim Iqbal are the openers. Donald Tiripano to bowl first up, to Tamim. Here we go...

Excellent self-belief and discipline from Bangladesh. At no point did they get frustrated, believing that the wicket will come at some point of time or the other and eventually, the dismissals did come. Everyone bowled well but Abu Jayed and Nayeem Hasan hogged the limelight with 4 wickets apiece. The bowlers will now hope to put their feet for at least 2 days in the pavilion.

Not the best bit of batting efforts from Zimbabwe. They started solidly, being 118/1 but then the middle order could not quite capitalize. Only three batsmen reached 30, which is never enough in Test cricket. On a slow deck, a minimum of 300 is necessary. They have fallen at least 40-50 runs short.

A bit of frustration for the home side but it eventually gets the work done. It has been hard work, they have toiled hard but ensured that not too many runs have been scored on this deck. The bowling has been excellent, keeping things tight.

The umpires are slowly making their way out to the middle. Now, the Bangladeshi players get into a huddle. They are followed by the overnight Zimbabwean batsmen - Donala Tiripano and Regis Chakabva. Abu Jayed to kick start proceedings to Tiripano. Here we go...
PITCH REPORT - The pitch has developed some cracks and there will be some turn. Early in the morning, there will be some seam movement.

A slow sluggish day of play is what we witnessed on Saturday. Bangladesh stifled Zimbabwe but the visitors managed to see off the day by fighting hard. But they have not quite got a decent score. Can they get to 300 at least? That will be a good score on this deck. Hello and a warm welcome to the second day of the one-off Test between Bangladesh and Zimbabwe in Dhaka.
So that is it from us today. Do join us on 23rd February, 2020 for Day 2 of this one-off Test. It will begin at 0930 local (0330 GMT). Till then take care and cheers!

On the other hand, Bangladesh bowlers did keep it tight. Nayeem Hasan was the star for them as he picked 4 wickets. The youngster was brilliant with his bowling. Taijul Islam was less effective. The pacers also bowled their heart out but only Abu Jayed picked two wickets.

This session has been a good one for both the teams. For Zimbabwe, Craig Ervine got to his hundred. He was brilliant throughout the day. He got out at the fag end of the day. Also Prince Masvaure was brilliant with the bat. His partnership with Craig Ervine was crucial.

Welcome back for the afternoon session. The two Zimbabwe batsmen Craig Ervine and Prince Masvaure walk out to the middle to resume their innings. Bangladesh players are also out and are in all readiness to start the session. Nayeem Hasan will start the proceedings.
... Day 1, Session 2 ...

Bangladesh's bowling was superb with both the opening bowlers being spot on. They beat the bat of the Zimbabwean batsmen frequently and Abu Jayed got into the wickets column. Since the introduction of spinners, the runs have started to leak. Will Bangladesh strike after the break or will Zimbabwe continue to grind it out in the middle? Join us for the afternoon session in a while.

A good session of Test match cricket. It started slowly and then picked up pace. Zimbabwe won the toss and elected to bat first on a wicket which had an even covering of grass. The two openers Prince Masvaure and Kevin Kasuza started watchfully as they played out the opening bowlers by defending anything which was in line with the stumps. They picked up pace gradually and started scoring briskly. In the process they lost Kasuza to Abu Jayed but since then, skipper Craig Ervine and Prince Masvaure have steadied the ship with a gritty stand of 73 runs. Both the batsmen were severe on the spinners as they swept and reverse swept them constantly.

Bangladesh skipper, Mominul Haque says that they would have batted first as well. He adds that the first innings will be crucial and they would look to restrict Zimbabwe early on. Further says that there is something in the wicket for the spinners.

Zimbabwe skipper, Craig Ervine says that they will bat first. He adds that there is a lot of green grass and the first session will be crucial. He also mentions that it looks a pretty decent wicket and everything will depend on how the first session pans out for them.
TOSS - Zimbabwe win the toss and elect to bat.

Hello and a warm welcome to the one-off Test between Bangladesh and Zimbabwe in Mirpur. The hosts experienced a tough time in Pakistan and would like to start afresh at home. On the other hand, Zimbabwe showed great heart in their last Test match against Sri Lanka back home and would like to make the most of this exposure of playing a Test match in Asian conditions. Without doubt, Bangladesh will be the favourites but they cannot afford to take the African minnows lightly.
